page: Amazon Web Services r8id.96xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 384 vCPUs across 192 physical cores using the x86_64 architecture, specifically utilizing Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors running at 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 3072.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of 22800 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in multi-core CPU execution, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Passmark CPU tests, including encryption and physics. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also rank in the top 10%. Database operations and Redis SET operations achieve top-tier throughput, with Redis reaching 451.6 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core results falling into the middle 50% and Geekbench single-core scores in the top 25%.

While the instance excels at large-scale parallel processing, a notable performance tradeoff exists in low-resource LLM text generation; text generation for a small 135M model ranks in the bottom 10%, whereas prompt processing for medium 7B models reaches the top 10%. Given the combination of massive DDR5 memory, high-capacity local NVMe SSD storage, and 100 Gbps network bandwidth, this server is configured for memory-intensive databases, large-scale data caching, and enterprise-level database operations.
